text:
Leah: Quick proposal — add a first-class 'presets' layer to the quant profile API so ops and customers can pick vetted bundles (e.g. 'fp8-latency', 'int8-safety') instead of hand-editing per-tensor rules.
Rafael: I like the ergonomics. How do we handle ops that must stay FP32 (softmax/gelu)?
Leah: Each preset would include an allowlist + a force_fp32 list. Default presets set conservative force lists. Users can extend but we warn in console and tie to canary.
Priya: Telemetry question — we need per-preset degradation scores and per-op heatmaps. Is that part of the runtime contract?
Leah: Yes — runtime emits preset_id + per-op degradation metrics and a confidence score. Backend aggregates by customer and by endpoint.
Jon: Rollout playbook: canary preset on shadow traffic, compare degscore + latency, then staged rollout with automatic rollback if degscore delta > threshold.
Leah: Exactly. Also propose an 'escape hatch' toggle that forces FP32 for a preset for a customer when they hit an incident.
Rafael: Edge case: attention kernels with custom CUDA paths — if preset flips those to int8 we may need kernel compatibility metadata.
Leah: plan: preset includes 'compat_tags' and runtime validates kernel availability before activating. If missing, runtime falls back to a compatible preset or blocks activation.
Priya: Ops UI idea — show a small badge next to preset with expected latency delta and estimated cost delta based on offline profiling.
Jon: For canary testing, we should expose a CLI: `ri presets canary --preset fp8-latency --endpoint chat-prod --shadow 10%` — ops-bot could automate traffic split and diff tests.
ops-bot: deploybot: Canary job queued for preset fp8-latency on chat-prod at 10% shadow. ID=cp-1758214321-1 :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Leah: Security/compliance note — presets must be bound to model versions. You cannot apply a preset to a mismatched model arch without explicit opt-in. Add model_signature to preset metadata.
Rafael: How about migration: existing per-tensor profiles -> generate a 'custom' preset during import and mark it unrated until we run sampling evs.
Priya: Sampling evs: schedule a shadow run for a week, compute degscore and token drift, then auto-classify preset as safe/warn/unsafe.
Jon: Operational knobs: allow customer override but require a signed acceptance if they opt for an 'unsafe' preset (legal/compliance).
Leah: Impl steps: 1) API + schema for preset objects 2) runtime validation + compat_tags 3) telemetry hooks + degscore per op 4) UI/CLI for canary + rollback 5) migration tool to convert existing profiles.
Rafael: Sounds good. Can we split into two PRs: schema + migration first, runtime validation + telemetry second? That keeps risk lower.
Leah: Agreed. I'll open an RFC follow-up with a prioritized checklist and owners.
Priya: Also add a small hook for evals team to register per-preset evaluation prompts so we can detect quality regressions early.
Leah: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
